claims.text: Atomic-size mismatch controls phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Al is the primary source of the relevant atomic-size mismatch in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni.
Atomic-size mismatch tunes the balance between mixing entropy and the enthalpy of ordering.
A modest Al level promotes lattice distortion.
Al-induced lattice distortion suppresses formation of brittle ordered or precipitate phases.
A modest Al level preserves sufficient local disorder to maintain a single-phase structure.
Excessive Al promotes local chemical ordering or precipitate formation.
Al-induced ordering or precipitation compromises the targeted combination of properties.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni is primarily a single-phase disordered FCC or BCC alloy.
Al-enhanced lattice distortion raises free-energy barriers for ordering or phase separation.
At an optimal Al content, the alloy remains single phase because little mixing entropy is sacrificed while ordering enthalpy is suppressed.
The proposed balance of lattice distortion, defect activity, and phase stability is beneficial to alloy performance.
An optimally adjusted Al composition will remain single phase relative to the equiatomic baseline.
An optimally adjusted Al composition will have greater high-temperature strength than the equiatomic baseline.
An optimally adjusted Al composition will have greater environmental resistance than the equiatomic baseline.
An optimally adjusted Al composition will have greater radiation tolerance than the equiatomic baseline.
An optimally adjusted Al composition will have greater cryogenic toughness than the equiatomic baseline.
